panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (a, b, c, d, e). a: MRI scan from a patient with Wolf-Hirschhorn syndrome showing hypogenesis of the corpus callosum and white matter dysmyelination, which are recognized CNS manifestations of the syndrome. b: MRI scan from a patient with Wolf-Hirschhorn syndrome demonstrating thin corpus callosum (hypogenesis) on sagittal T1, a classic brain malformation associated with the syndrome. c: MRI scan from a patient with Wolf-Hirschhorn syndrome showing lateral ventricle dilatation and hypogenesis of the corpus callosum, consistent with the syndrome's neuroimaging phenotype. d: MRI scan from a patient with Wolf-Hirschhorn syndrome (pt. no. 1) demonstrating defective myelination; the in-text confirms all patients had corpus callosum agenesis/hypogenesis, a core feature of the syndrome. e: MRI scan from a patient with Wolf-Hirschhorn syndrome showing thin corpus callosum (hypogenesis) on sagittal T2, a characteristic brain malformation of the syndrome.

in_text_mentions: Case 3 is a 2-year-old boy, second child of an unrelated, apparently healthy couple, with no similar cases in the family. Pregnancy evolved with intrauterine growth retardation. The child was born at 36 weeks, by cesarean section (Wt = 1400 g, Ht = 30 cm, OFC = 28 cm). Postnatal development is delayed. The last evaluation (1 Y 6 Mo) revealed small size (Wt: −7.09 SD, Ht: −5.7SD), microcephaly (OFC: −4.81 SD), characteristic dysmorphic face (Figure 1).
